audit.whatIsWrong: Three strings call Fate Sealed a 'double-knockup' that 'interrupts your Sundering Slam all-in' (spikes[3].text, whys[6], wants.foe[2]).
audit.why: Fate Sealed is not a knockup at all. Yone blinks BEHIND the last champion in a line and slashes, pulling everyone hit toward him — a displacement inward, on 120s at rank 1 from 1000 range. The practical difference is total: a knockup is something you eat where you stand, a pull is something that relocates you into his team, and the counterplay is spacing along his likely line rather than timing an interrupt. It is also worth naming that his R selects the LAST champion in the line while Ambessa's selects the FARTHEST in hers — two mirrored line-selection ultimates in one matchup, and neither layer says so.
audit.corrected: Fate Sealed (R), 120/100/80, 1000 range: he blinks behind the LAST champion in a line and pulls everyone hit toward him. Spread along the line, don't stack on it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yone.json — R Fate Sealed 'blinks behind the last champion in a line with a slash so powerful it pulls all enemies hit towards him', cd 120/100/80, flags dash only

audit.whatIsWrong: Spirit Cleave is called a 'W double-slash' in three strings and its shield is never mentioned anywhere in either layer.
audit.why: Spirit Cleave is a cone cleave that SHIELDS Yone, with the shield growing per champion hit, and both its cooldown and its cast time scale with his attack speed. That makes it the same class of problem as any shield against Ambessa: her damage arrives as one compressed Q-into-empowered-auto burst, and a fresh Spirit Cleave eats exactly that window. It also means the entry's own advice to fear his attack-speed scaling is understated — attack speed does not just raise his DPS, it shortens the cooldown on his shield. 'Double-slash' names nothing a player can find on the ability bar.
audit.corrected: Spirit Cleave (W), 14s base and shorter as he buys attack speed: a cone that shields him, scaling with champions hit. Bait the shield before you spend the burst.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yone.json — W Spirit Cleave 'Grants a shield to Yone, the value is increased by the number of champions hit... cooldown and cast time scale with attack speed', cd 14

audit.whatIsWrong: Soul Unbound is the tracked, matchup-defining ability and the pivot of every piece of advice on the page ('bait that button before you spend Cunning Sweep'), and its cooldown appears nowhere. Three strings also call Ambessa's empowered attack a 'Medarda-empowered auto'.
audit.why: Soul Unbound is 22 seconds at rank 1, dropping to 10 at rank 5, and it costs him nothing. Twenty-two seconds is what makes baiting it a real plan early and a much weaker one later, which is exactly the arc the entry is trying to describe without the number. Separately, 'Medarda' is Ambessa's surname, not an ability — the empowered attack comes from Drakehound's Step (P), and a player reading 'Medarda-empowered auto' has nothing to look for.
audit.corrected: Soul Unbound (E), 22/19/16/13/10, no cost. Drakehound's Step (P) is the passive that empowers her next attack.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yone.json — E Soul Unbound cd 22/19/16/13/10, cost 0

audit.whatIsWrong: content.late credits Ambessa with 'your R's armor-pen passive'. Yone's passive is also described only as 'on-hit/crit steroids'.
audit.why: Public Execution has no armour penetration in Riot's text — the kit file's flags on her R are tooltip-parsing misfires (see notes). And Way of the Hunter deals MAGIC damage on every second attack as well as raising his crit chance, which means his damage profile is mixed: stacking armour alone reads the trade wrong in a matchup where the entry's itemization already leans on Plated Steelcaps.
audit.corrected: Way of the Hunter (P): magic damage on every second attack, plus bonus crit chance — his damage is mixed, so armour alone is the wrong read.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yone.json — P Way of the Hunter 'deals magic damage with every second Attack'

edits.before: Yone owns the very first levels — his Q poke and W double-slash out-tempo your one energy-gated ability, so don't try to dash-weave before your level 3 combo is online. Last-hit with the tip of your Cunning Sweep cone (the outer edge deals double) and accept the chip; you can't win level 1 here. The trap is his E: he leaves his body, and recasting snaps him back to where he cast it while echoing a chunk of the damage he dealt — so if you commit a trade while he's holding E, he rewinds out and undoes much of your damage. Bait that button before you spend Cunning Sweep into Sundering Slam. By level 3 your cone-into-slam plus a Medarda-empowered auto gives you a real short-trade window — but only when his E is down.
edits.after: Yone owns the very first levels — Mortal Steel poke and a Spirit Cleave that shields him out-tempo your one energy-gated ability, so don't try to dash-weave before your level 3 combo is online. Last-hit with the tip of your Cunning Sweep cone (the outer edge deals double) and accept the chip; you can't win level 1 here. The trap is Soul Unbound: his spirit leaves the body, and it snaps back to where he cast it while echoing a chunk of the damage he dealt — so a trade you commit while he holds it gets partly undone. It is 22 seconds at rank 1, so baiting it out really does buy you a window. By level 3 your cone-into-slam plus a Drakehound's Step empowered auto is a real short trade — inside those 22 seconds.

edits.before: Your first-item spike (Eclipse/Profane plus level 9 Q max) still beats him in a straight fight — force all-ins here while you can. Your damage is entirely physical, and your R's armor-pen passive helps, but once he itemizes and his W cleave outranges your empowered-auto windows you stop pinning him down. Close this before he gets two items, or accept that he becomes the mobile carry you can't catch.
edits.after: Your first-item spike (Eclipse/Profane plus level 9 Q max) still beats him in a straight fight — force all-ins here while you can. notes: The packet flags this entry as 'never names any of Yone's abilities' — accurate for the CONTENT layer, which said 'his E', 'W double-slash', 'Q poke', 'third-Q knockup' and 'his R double-knockup' throughout. Two of those descriptions were not merely unnamed but wrong: Spirit Cleave shields him (never mentioned at all) and Fate Sealed pulls rather than knocking up. One good thing worth preserving: the existing spikes[2].text correctly reasons that Soul Unbound only rewinds him to where he cast it, so it cannot pull him out of a Public Execution suppress — that is sound against the kit text and I left it intact.
